accepted.s: Which of the following best describes e-Pragati in Andhra Pradesh?
o: A platform exclusively for agricultural subsidies
A whole-of-government programme interconnecting e-governance systems
accepted.x: e-Pragati is Andhra Pradesh’s whole-of-government programme under which e-governance systems are interconnected.
accepted.tq: Identify the broad institutional scope of the programme rather than a single service.
accepted.sec: AP flagship e-governance - e-Pragati, CARD, RTGS, BhuSeva, Mana Mitra  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a core dataset associated with e-Pragati?
accepted.x: The core e-Pragati datasets include People Hub, Land Hub, Entity Hub, GIS Hub and IoT Hub. Revenue Hub is not included in the listed set.
accepted.tq: Find the option that does not belong to the named group.
accepted.sec: AP flagship e-governance - e-Pragati, CARD, RTGS, BhuSeva, Mana Mitra  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: In February 2026, e-Pragati integrated how many additional citizen services, with the stated objective of promoting which model of governance?
o: 25 services; transparent, accountable and decentralised governance
45 services; faceless, paperless and cashless governance
accepted.x: In February 2026, 45 more citizen services were integrated into e-Pragati, with the objective of faceless, paperless and cashless governance.
accepted.tq: Split the option into the numerical figure and the associated phrase.
accepted.sec: AP flagship e-governance - e-Pragati, CARD, RTGS, BhuSeva, Mana Mitra  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Which of the following technologies or facilities is associated with the Real Time Governance Society in Andhra Pradesh?
1. Artificial Intelligence
2. Big Data
3. Geographic Information System
4. Real-time dashboards
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Real Time Governance Society uses Artificial Intelligence, Big Data, GIS, IoT and real-time dashboards. All four listed items are associated with it.
accepted.tq: Use the inclusive technology list and check whether any item is outside the stated scope.
accepted.sec: AP flagship e-governance - e-Pragati, CARD, RTGS, BhuSeva, Mana Mitra  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Real Time Governance Society:
1. It uses a Data Lake and Data Lens.
2. It operates through a Command and Control Centre.
3. Nara Lokesh is the minister in charge.
4. The Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026–27 allocated approximately ₹100 crore to it.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Real Time Governance Society is associated with Data Lake, Data Lens, a Command and Control Centre, Nara Lokesh as minister in charge, and an approximately ₹100 crore allocation in the 2026–27 Budget.
accepted.tq: Test a cluster of closely related institutional, technological and budget facts.
accepted.sec: AP flagship e-governance - e-Pragati, CARD, RTGS, BhuSeva, Mana Mitra  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: BhuSeva in Andhra Pradesh is primarily associated with which of the following?
accepted.x: BhuSeva is an Andhra Pradesh integrated land-records platform.
accepted.tq: Match the platform with its principal service domain.
accepted.sec: AP flagship e-governance - e-Pragati, CARD, RTGS, BhuSeva, Mana Mitra  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about Mana Mitra is correct?
1. More than 500 services were enabled at its launch.
2. Its Outcome Budget target envisaged up to 1,000 services.
3. It uses WhatsApp as a channel for conversational governance.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Mana Mitra enabled more than 500 services, used WhatsApp-based conversational governance, and had an Outcome Budget target of up to 1,000 services.
accepted.tq: Check whether the numerical targets and operational feature consistently describe the same initiative.
accepted.sec: AP flagship e-governance - e-Pragati, CARD, RTGS, BhuSeva, Mana Mitra  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The expression ‘MeeSeva’ literally means:
accepted.x: MeeSeva means ‘At your service’ in Telugu.
accepted.tq: Test the exact meaning of a public-service brand name.
accepted.sec: MeeSeva - meaning, launch, service categories, delivery model  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes MeeSeva?
o: It was launched in 2001 as the successor to e-Seva.
It was launched in 2019 as a replacement for Gram Sachivalayam.
It was launched in 2011 in undivided Andhra Pradesh as the successor to e-Seva.
It was launched in 2025 as a WhatsApp-based service.
accepted.x: MeeSeva was launched in 2011 in undivided Andhra Pradesh and succeeded e-Seva, which began in 2001.
accepted.tq: Separate the launch year and predecessor from nearby e-governance initiatives.
accepted.sec: MeeSeva - meaning, launch, service categories, delivery model  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following was the first integrated citizen service-centre initiative in India and preceded MeeSeva?
accepted.x: e-Seva, launched in 2001, was the first integrated citizen service-centre initiative in India and preceded MeeSeva.
accepted.tq: Use the predecessor relationship to distinguish related programmes.
accepted.sec: MeeSeva - meaning, launch, service categories, delivery model  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Which of the following services can be delivered through MeeSeva centres?
1. Caste certificates
2. Income certificates
3. Residence certificates
4. Land-record extracts
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: MeeSeva centres provide certificates such as caste, income and residence certificates, along with land-record extracts and registration-linked services.
accepted.tq: Recognise the common service-delivery basket rather than a single category.
accepted.sec: MeeSeva - meaning, launch, service categories, delivery model  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The delivery model of MeeSeva is based primarily on:
o: Direct service delivery only through district collectors
Single-window service delivery through MeeSeva centres
accepted.x: MeeSeva follows a single-window service-delivery model through MeeSeva centres.
accepted.tq: Identify the operational model from the citizen’s point of access.
accepted.sec: MeeSeva - meaning, launch, service categories, delivery model  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: SDC stands for State Data Centre. SWAN means State Wide Area Network, MMP means Mission Mode Project and DACNET means Department of Agriculture and Cooperation Network.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure expansion and reject look-alike full forms.
accepted.sec: Full forms of e-gov platforms (UMANG, CARD, NeGP, MMP, SWAN, SDC, DACNET)  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The abbreviation ‘NeGP’ stands for:
accepted.x: NeGP is the National e-Governance Plan.
accepted.tq: Test the exact official expansion of an administrative abbreviation.
accepted.sec: Full forms of e-gov platforms (UMANG, CARD, NeGP, MMP, SWAN, SDC, DACNET)  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: DACNET — Department of Agriculture and Cooperation Network
CPGRAMS — Centralized Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System
e-Taal — Electronic Transactions Aggregation and Analysis Layer
accepted.x: MMP stands for Mission Mode Project, not Mission Monitoring Portal. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Find the deceptively plausible expansion that changes the official wording.
accepted.sec: Full forms of e-gov platforms (UMANG, CARD, NeGP, MMP, SWAN, SDC, DACNET)  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The 28th National Conference on e-Governance, held in 2025, was organised at:
accepted.x: The 28th National Conference on e-Governance in 2025 was held at Visakhapatnam.
accepted.tq: Test the venue of a named national conference against nearby administrative locations.
accepted.sec: National Conference and National Awards on e-Governance  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The 28th National Conference on e-Governance was organised by DARPG in association with:
o: NITI Aayog and the Reserve Bank of India
The Election Commission and the host district
UNDP and the Ministry of Home Affairs
accepted.x: The conference was organised by the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances with the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology and the host State.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct institutional partners instead of substituting neighbouring government bodies.
accepted.sec: National Conference and National Awards on e-Governance  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: National Awards for e-Governance are given by:
accepted.x: The National Awards for e-Governance are given by the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG).
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘who gives the award?’ authority check.
accepted.sec: National Conference and National Awards on e-Governance  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding e-governance-related initiatives?
1. DARPG’s State Collaboration Initiatives, revised in 2015–16, support replication of selected award-winning initiatives.
2. NeSDA benchmarking started in 2019.
3. The State Collaboration Initiatives support replication of initiatives awarded by the Prime Minister and through National Awards for e-Governance.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The State Collaboration Initiatives were revised in 2015–16 and support replication of PM-awarded and National e-Governance-awarded initiatives; NeSDA benchmarking began in 2019.
accepted.tq: Combine the date, institutional programme and purpose before selecting the coded option.
accepted.sec: National Conference and National Awards on e-Governance  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the four phases of the Gartner model?
accepted.x: The four Gartner phases are Information, Interaction, Transaction and Transformation, in that order.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact ordered framework rather than merely identifying its individual terms.
accepted.sec: E-governance concepts - Gartner model, pillars, G2C/G2B/G2G, role of ICT  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Open Government Data — DBT for LPG subsidy
accepted.x: G2E is illustrated by CEMS, an employee-management system. G2P is illustrated by DBT, Open Government Data by data.gov.in, and m-Governance by services such as mPassport Seva and UMANG.
accepted.tq: Match each governance relationship with its specific example.
accepted.sec: E-governance concepts - Gartner model, pillars, G2C/G2B/G2G, role of ICT  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following is an example of G2P (Government-to-Person) service?
o: DBT for LPG subsidy and pensions
accepted.x: Direct Benefit Transfer for LPG subsidies and pensions is an example of G2P service delivery.
accepted.tq: Infer the relationship from the recipient of the service or benefit.
accepted.sec: E-governance concepts - Gartner model, pillars, G2C/G2B/G2G, role of ICT  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is associated with m-Governance?
o: Data Lake and Data Lens only
accepted.x: mPassport Seva and UMANG are examples of m-Governance. The m-Governance framework dates to 2012, while MSDG dates to 2011.
accepted.tq: Identify the mobile-governance examples and distinguish them from infrastructure platforms.
accepted.sec: E-governance concepts - Gartner model, pillars, G2C/G2B/G2G, role of ICT  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the three vision areas of Digital India mentioned below?
o: Digital infrastructure as a core utility
accepted.x: The three listed Digital India vision areas are digital infrastructure as a core utility, governance and services on demand, and digital empowerment of citizens.
accepted.tq: Reject an extreme policy claim that is outside the stated vision areas.
accepted.sec: E-governance concepts - Gartner model, pillars, G2C/G2B/G2G, role of ICT  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following best expresses the role of ICT in e-governance?
o: It prevents real-time monitoring of public services.
It enhances citizen engagement and improves service delivery.
It replaces all government institutions with private agencies.
It limits citizen participation to physical offices.
accepted.x: ICT enhances citizen engagement and improves service delivery, including through transparency and real-time monitoring.
accepted.tq: Choose the option that states the positive functional role rather than an absolute consequence.
accepted.sec: E-governance concepts - Gartner model, pillars, G2C/G2B/G2G, role of ICT  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. ICT can promote transparency in governance.
2. Real-time monitoring is facilitated by technology-enabled governance.
3. Internet shutdowns can disrupt digital public services.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Technology can improve transparency and real-time monitoring, while internet shutdowns can disrupt services that depend on digital connectivity.
accepted.tq: Check both the enabling and disruptive effects of ICT on service delivery.
accepted.sec: E-governance concepts - Gartner model, pillars, G2C/G2B/G2G, role of ICT  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with its role in NeGP infrastructure?
o: SDC — converged backbone for data, voice and video
CSC — hosts State e-governance applications and data
accepted.x: Common Service Centres are village-level front-end delivery outlets. SWAN is the converged backbone network, while SDC hosts State e-governance applications and data.
accepted.tq: Match each infrastructure pillar with its functional layer.
accepted.sec: NeGP infrastructure - SWAN, State Data Centres, Common Service Centres  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The principal role of SWAN is to provide:
o: A secure repository exclusively for land records
A converged backbone network for data, voice and video across the State
A cloud platform for private companies
accepted.x: SWAN, or State Wide Area Network, provides a converged backbone network for data, voice and video across the State.
accepted.tq: Identify the network-layer function rather than the application or front-end function.
accepted.sec: NeGP infrastructure - SWAN, State Data Centres, Common Service Centres  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: A State Data Centre primarily performs which function?
o: Provides only mobile applications to citizens
Hosts State e-governance applications and data on common secure IT infrastructure
Acts as a village-level kiosk network
accepted.x: The State Data Centre hosts State e-governance applications and data on common secure IT infrastructure.
accepted.tq: Determine the infrastructure function from the location and type of digital resource hosted.
accepted.sec: NeGP infrastructure - SWAN, State Data Centres, Common Service Centres  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about SWAN, SDC and CSC is correct?
1. SWAN functions as a State-wide backbone network.
2. SDC provides common secure infrastructure for hosting applications and data.
3. CSCs operate as village-level front-end delivery outlets.
4. Together, they enable G2G, G2C and G2B services.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four statements correctly describe the roles of SWAN, SDC and CSCs and their combined contribution to G2G, G2C and G2B service delivery.
accepted.tq: Test the complete infrastructure chain from backbone and hosting to citizen-facing delivery.
accepted.sec: NeGP infrastructure - SWAN, State Data Centres, Common Service Centres  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the relationship among G2G, G2C and G2B services and NeGP infrastructure?
o: They are enabled only by CSCs without any network or hosting infrastructure.
They are enabled together by SWAN, SDC and CSC.
They refer exclusively to mobile governance applications.
They are unrelated to State Data Centres.
accepted.x: SWAN, State Data Centres and Common Service Centres together enable seamless Government-to-Government, Government-to-Citizen and Government-to-Business services.
accepted.tq: Link each service relationship to the complete infrastructure stack instead of one component alone.
accepted.sec: NeGP infrastructure - SWAN, State Data Centres, Common Service Centres  [GROUP-II]
